transcript: 00:00 Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — sound and video ok?
00:05 Maya Chen: Yep all good, thanks Alex.
00:08 Priya Singh: Morning! I'll start with a quick recap of what we ran last week — we pushed the SDK change that pins structured output schema and flipped tool calling for the payments lookup flow.

00:20 John Liu: Right, we ran three batches against staging, saw about a 10% drop in parsing errors but a couple of edge cases where the JSON still comes back malformed, like missing fields and occasionally a nested array showing up where we expect a map.
00:34 Alex Morgan: Ok, do you have examples of the exact prompts that caused it? Sometimes the template spacing or trailing punctuation trips the parser — can you paste one or two?

00:45 John Liu: Yeah I'll paste after the call, but one example is the refund flow where the amount is optional in the prompt, the model returned an empty string for amount and we lose the key entirely.

00:58 Priya Singh: Mm hm, that sounds like the model generating an empty token rather than null. We have two short fixes — one is to add explicit guard fields in the schema like "amount_nullable:true" and the other is to run a post-parse reconciliation step in the SDK that fills defaults.
01:14 Maya Chen: Which is better long term? We prefer minimal client-side logic if the model can be coaxed to be deterministic.

01:22 Priya Singh: Ideally the structured-output constraint plus a short system instruction to always emit keys even if blank works, but we still recommend the small SDK safeguard as a safety net for production.

01:32 Ravi Patel: Side note on tool calling — we tried using the DB-tool path via your tool-caller, and the auth flow fails intermittently from our staging VPC. It looks like token rotation plus our NAT gateway timeouts are interfering.

01:47 Alex Morgan: Got it. For VPC-deployed pilots we usually recommend using a short-lived signed URL pattern or a service account with mTLS. We can walk through the KMS-based signing flow during the VPC deep-dive. Priya, do we have a runbook?

01:58 Priya Singh: Yes, I've got a doc with 2 options — (1) token rotation with our SDK helper, (2) mTLS + mutual TLS handshake using customer certs. I'll link it after. For the NAT timeouts, Ravi, can you share the egress policy?
02:12 Ravi Patel: I'll share the AWS route tables and NAT config. We may need to allow longer idle timeouts on the NAT or use a proxy in front.
02:20 John Liu: Back to model behavior — when we switch to a smaller open model to save cost, the structured output quality dropped more than expected. Any guidance on quantization / model variant?

02:32 Priya Singh: Yep, smaller quantized variants are cost savers but noisier. For structured output we recommend a two-tier approach: use the higher-fidelity model for the final parse step, and a smaller cheap model for the candidate generation if you need suggestions. Also, tuning the temperature down to 0.0–0.2 and increasing the max tokens buffer helps.
02:50 Maya Chen: Can Redwood handle that split automatically? Routing generation vs parse to different model variants?

02:56 Alex Morgan: Absolutely — our smart routing can route by route or by step. We'll show you an example where the SDK calls the generator on a low-cost model and then posts the candidate to a high-fidelity verifier model before structured parsing.
03:10 John Liu: Nice. About latency — that two-step will increase L96 latencies sometimes. For our user flows we target sub-300ms on median; current staging with the verifier is around 420ms median.

03:22 Priya Singh: Two knobs: batching and KV cache. For interactive flows, disable batching or set max batch size to 1 and enable prefix caching. Also check your sequence length — shorter prompts are big wins. We'll run the benchmark with and without the verifier so you can see tradeoffs.
03:36 Maya Chen: That would be helpful — we care about both cost and user perception. If latency jumps over 500ms we lose conversions.
03:42 Alex Morgan: Understood. We'll produce a CSV with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens for each config.
03:48 Ravi Patel: Another small issue — when tool calling triggers DB writes, we want audit logs and idempotency keys. Can Redwood attach request IDs and preserve trace context?

03:58 Priya Singh: Yes — the SDK can inject request_id and preserve X-Request-ID headers across tool calls. We also emit trace hooks to the console; if you want we can stream traces to your Splunk/Datadog via our connector.
04:09 John Liu: Perfect — that solves compliance concerns. On the security front Maya had asked about SOC2 and KMS — anything new?

04:16 Alex Morgan: We shared the SOC2 Type II and the KMS integration guide in the security pack last week. For KMS we can either use customer-managed keys in our hosted flow or if you're on Private we can inject into your KMS.
04:26 Maya Chen: We're evaluating Private but timeline depends on legal. For pilot we need RBAC and retention settings. Can we set retention to 30 days and enforce redaction?
04:34 Priya Singh: Yes, retention is configurable per project. We also support automatic redaction rules — we can apply PII scrubbing on ingest for the pilot.
04:42 Alex Morgan: Quick recap — action items and we'll reconvene next week. Anything else urgent?
04:47 John Liu: One small ask — can you add a sample of the SDK call that shows the fallback when the structured parse fails? We want to see preferred semantics.
04:55 Priya Singh: Yes, I'll add a snippet showing try-parse, fallback heuristics, and a small deterministic canonicalizer.
05:01 Maya Chen: Great. Also please include estimated cost delta for enabling the verifier model at our current volume (~50k monthly active prompts).
05:09 Alex Morgan: We'll put that in the benchmark doc. Ok thanks everyone — we'll send the links and schedule the VPC deep-dive. Talk next week.
05:18 Maya Chen: Thanks all, bye.
05:20 Alex Morgan: Bye.
